claim_a_text: Sliding-window detection with deep CNNs is challenging due to large receptive fields and strides, making precise localization difficult.
claim_b_text: A fully convolutional sliding-window approach (RPN) is effective for generating region proposals and enables precise localization.
claim_a_quote: units high up in our network, which has five convolutional layers, have very large receptive fields (195 × 195 pixels) and strides (32×32 pixels) in the input image, which makes precise localization within the sliding-window paradigm an open technical challenge.
claim_b_quote: An RPN is a fully convolutional network that simultaneously predicts object bounds and objectness scores at each position.
rationale: ARTICLE_A explicitly states that sliding-window detection with deep CNNs is challenging for precise localization, while ARTICLE_B introduces an RPN, a fully convolutional sliding-window network, as an effective solution for generating region proposals and predicting object bounds, representing a nuanced architectural disagreement on the feasibility of sliding-window approaches in deep CNNs.
